name: Punan Tubu
world_status: a description exists but is not accessible

earlier_scan.verdict: a source was named but could not be reached
earlier_scan.source_named: Antonia Soriente's Punan Tubu' documentation (dictionary and sketch materials, ca. 2006-2020); plausibly covers stress; not found openly online at scan time

sources.citation: Soriente, Antonia. 2018. Deixis in Borneo: Kenyah and Punan. Ethnorema 14 (author preprint, UNIOR IRIS hdl 11574/184438).
sources.note: Demonstrative systems of Kenyah and Punan Tubu'; silent on stress.

sources.citation: Sellato, Bernard. 2017. Review of N. Cesard, A. Guerreiro & A. Soriente (eds), Petualangan Unjung dan Mbui Kuvong: Sastra lisan dan kamus Punan Tuvu' dari Kalimantan (Jakarta: EFEO & KPG, 2015). Wacana 18(1): 266-268. DOI 10.17510/wacana.v18i1.581 (HAL halshs-02542193).
sources.note: Nothing on stress itself; establishes that the 2015 book contains Soriente's 'brief description of Punan Tubu language (pp. 47-62), successively examining its phonology and morphology', that Dollop Mamung described 'Fonologi bahasa daerah Dayak Punan Tubu' in his 1981 BA (S1) thesis, and that a 1998 KRC (WWF, Samarinda) Punan Tubu dictionary by Dollop Mamung preceded the 2015 volume.

sources.citation: Smith, Alexander D. 2017. The languages of Borneo: a comprehensive classification. PhD dissertation, University of Hawai'i at Manoa.
sources.access_detail: a digital copy (available on request); access check: not located online or in the libraries checked
sources.note: Own fieldwork wordlist for Punan Tubu (Respen Tubu) and Proto-Punan historical phonology (sec. 2.4.3); stress is discussed only for Merap, Segai-Modang, Hliboi Bidayuh and West Kalimantan Malayic; nothing on Punan Tubu stress.

sources.citation: Soriente, Antonia. 2014. Studying linguistic and cultural contact in Borneo: prospects and challenges. Antropologia n.s. 1(1): 59-81.
sources.note: Classification (shared phonological innovations of Kayan-Kenyah, Punan position) and contact; silent on stress in Punan Tubu.

sources.citation: Soriente, Antonia. 2013. Endangered oral literature genres in Punan Tubu (East Kalimantan). In Proceedings of the International Workshop on 'Special Genres' in and around Indonesia. Tokyo: ILCAA, TUFS, pp. 151-166.
sources.note: Discusses verse structure (8-syllable lines, rhyme/assonance) of keledu', ketuya', ledun; no statement about lexical stress placement.

sources.citation: Soriente, Antonia. 2013. Undergoer voice in Borneo: Penan, Punan, Kenyah and Kayan languages. In A. Adelaar (ed.), Voice variation in Austronesian languages of Indonesia. NUSA 54: 175-203.
sources.note: Morphosyntax of voice in Punan Tubu' and neighbours; only morphophonology of the nasal prefix; silent on word stress.

sources.citation: Soriente, Antonia. 2013. Variation in aspect and modality in some languages of Northeastern Borneo. NUSA 55: 193-218.
sources.note: Section 4 'Punan Tubu'' gives speaker numbers, location (Respen Tubu, Malinau) and TAM markers; no phonology; silent on stress.

sources.citation: Cesard, Nicolas. 2007. A sociohistorical transition: trade in forest products and bride-price among the Punan Tubu of Eastern Kalimantan. Anthropos 102: 455-477 (HAL hal-00178609).
sources.note: Social anthropology; no language/orthography notes; silent on stress.

sources.citation: Soriente, Antonia. 2015. Catatan Tata Bahasa Punan Tuvu'. In N. Cesard, A. Guerreiro & A. Soriente (eds), Petualangan Unjung dan Mbui Kuvong: Sastra lisan dan kamus Punan Tuvu' dari Kalimantan (Naskah dan Dokumen Nusantara XXXV), pp. 47-62. Jakarta: Ecole francaise d'Extreme-Orient & Kepustakaan Populer Gramedia. ISBN 978-979-91-0976-7 / 978-2-85539-197-7.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.access_detail: print only (no digital copy found when the work was looked up)
sources.note: The only modern first-hand grammar sketch of Punan Tuvu'; Sellato's review and the UNIOR abstract confirm it opens with a phonology ('deskripsi fonetis') section, the natural home of a stress/tekanan statement. In Indonesian, 16 pp.

sources.citation: Soriente, Antonia. 2026. Language documentation in Indonesia: directions, approaches, and case studies in Kalimantan and beyond. In Indonesian Languages and Linguistics, 52-74. Cornell UP / De Gruyter.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: Most recent Soriente overview with Kalimantan case studies (Punan Tuvu' is her main documentation language); low chance of a phonological profile but would supersede older remarks if present.

sources.citation: Soriente, Antonia. 2020. Hunter-gatherers of Borneo and the case study of the Penan Benalui. In T. Gueldemann, P. McConvell & R. Rhodes (eds), The Language of Hunter-Gatherers, 262-308. Cambridge University Press. ISBN 978-1-107-00368-2.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: Same author compares Penan Benalui with Punan Tubu'; a typological profile there could include a one-line stress remark for Punan Tubu' (second-best if the 2015 sketch stays closed).

sources.citation: Dollop Mamung. 1998. Punan Tubu' - Indonesian dictionary (KRC 'Dictionaries' series). Samarinda: Pusat Kebudayaan dan Alam Kalimantan (Kalimantan Resource Center), WWF Indonesia. [exact title not verified; existence per Sellato 2017: 'two 1998 KRC volumes by Drs Dollop Mamung on the language and folk literature of the Punan Tubu']

sources.note: Predecessor of the 2015 dictionary; front matter on spelling/phonology may state stress; copy reportedly held at Rumah Bhakti Lestari library, Balikpapan.

sources.citation: Dollop Mamung. 1981. Fonologi bahasa daerah Dayak Punan Tubu. Skripsi S1 (BA thesis); institution not stated in Sellato 2017 (presumably Samarinda).
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: A dedicated phonology of Punan Tubu by a native-speaker linguist; a Pusat Bahasa-style skripsi of this period normally has a 'fonem suprasegmental / tekanan' section stating stress placement.
